tools.description: Adds user-requested free-form feedback to the Cactal product-feedback inbox. Describe what happened and what would have made the experience better. Agents must set `authorKind` to `agent` even when acting through a user OAuth connection. Never include credentials, secrets, raw sensitive user content, or unnecessary personal or customer data.

authorKind.description: Who wrote the feedback. An AI agent must pass "agent" even when connected through a user OAuth token.

feedback.description: Concise free-form feedback describing the Cactal problem or limitation and what would have made the experience better.

tools.name: feedback_submit
tools.title: Submit product feedback

tools.description: Lists accessible websites. By default returns active websites: use `organizationId` to scope one organization, `scope=shared` without it for direct grants outside your memberships, or `scope=all` with it to combine both; supports `sort` by `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, or `name` and case-insensitive `search`, and each item includes `organizationSlug`, `primaryHostname`, and whether it is `shared`. Pass `status=deleted` with `organizationId` (requires organization-level trash access) to list restorable soft-deleted websites instead, each with its deletion time and purge deadline; deleted rows drop out when their 30-day restore window expires. Both modes use cursor pagination (default 20 per page, maximum 100). Fetch one website with `websites.get`.

status.description: Which websites to list. Defaults to `active`. `deleted` returns the organization’s restorable soft-deleted websites (requires `organizationId` and organization-level trash access) with their deletion time and purge deadline.

tools.name: websites_list
tools.title: List websites

tools.description: Returns a single website by `websiteId`, or by its `organizationSlug` + `websiteSlug` pair when starting from a URL — provide exactly one of the two identifications. The response includes whether the caller can manage the website’s CMS schema and domains. Websites in the trash remain retrievable by id (see `websites.list` with `status=deleted` for their purge timing); slug lookups only resolve active websites, and inaccessible or deleted resources return 404.

organizationSlug.description: URL slug of the owning organization. Pair with `websiteSlug` to look the website up by slug instead of id.

websiteId.description: Website id. Provide either this or the `organizationSlug` + `websiteSlug` pair.

websiteSlug.description: Website URL slug within the organization. Pair with `organizationSlug`.

tools.name: websites_get
tools.title: Get a website

tools.description: Creates a website in the organization. Provide either a `name` (trimmed, 1–200 characters) or a creation `prompt`; a prompt returns immediately with the temporary name `Untitled site`, which the built-in naming request attempts to replace on its next run together with a matching available slug and platform hostname. The hostname receives a short suffix when the clean hostname is unavailable. An omitted `slug` is allocated from the initial name; an explicit slug must be lowercase, URL-safe, unreserved, and unique among active websites in the organization. The website starts as an unpublished draft at `headVersion` 1. Send an `idempotencyKey` to make retries return the same website. Edit its source through the Source code operations, then publish with `websiteSourceCode.head.publish`.

idempotencyKey.description: Caller-generated key, such as a UUID, that makes creation safe to retry. Send the same key on every retry of one creation attempt: when this organization already has a website created with the key, that website is returned and no second website is created. A key whose website is in the trash returns a 409 with `idempotencyKeyStatus: "deleted"`; retry with a new key.

tools.name: websites_create
tools.title: Create a website

tools.description: Updates the website’s display name and, when supplied, its URL slug. The slug must be lowercase, URL-safe, unreserved, and unique among active websites in the organization.
tools.name: websites_rename
tools.title: Rename a website

tools.description: Returns every domain record attached to the website, oldest first: the automatically allocated platform subdomain plus any custom domains. Platform subdomains are always `active`; custom domains carry their current verification status and the DNS records still expected.
tools.name: websiteDomains_list
tools.title: List domains for a website

tools.description: Claims `hostname` for this website and registers it with the Cactal edge. Custom domains must first be enabled for the website (`websiteDomains.setEnabled`, owner-only — enabling is the billing moment); the request fails with 403 `custom_domains_disabled` otherwise. Adding or removing domains on an enabled website never changes billing. The domain is created in `pending_dns` status, and the returned `dnsRecords` list exactly what to create at your DNS provider: an ownership TXT record on `_cactal.<hostname>` plus a routing record (a CNAME for subdomains or an A record for apex domains). Hostnames must be lowercase ASCII domains (not IP addresses or Cactal platform hosts), each website can have at most 10 custom domains, and a hostname can be claimed by only one website; claims that never verify expire after 7 days. After creating the records, call the verify endpoint or wait for the automatic re-checks.
tools.name: websiteDomains_createCustomDomain
tools.title: Add a custom domain

tools.description: Re-checks the ownership TXT record, edge readiness, and whether an HTTPS request to the hostname reaches this Cactal domain, then returns the updated status. A customer CDN or reverse proxy in front is supported when it forwards the verification request to Cactal. `failureMessage` distinguishes a missing ownership record, an unreachable hostname, and a hostname served somewhere else. Cactal asks the domain nameservers directly, so new records usually count on the next check, and this endpoint is safe to poll; Cactal also re-checks pending domains automatically (every minute for the first 2 hours, every 5 minutes for the first day, then every 15 minutes). The first custom domain to become active is promoted to primary automatically.
tools.name: websiteDomains_verifyCustomDomain
tools.title: Verify a custom domain

tools.description: Makes this domain the canonical hostname for the published website: requests reaching the platform subdomain or any other custom domain are permanently redirected (HTTP 308) to it, preserving path and query. Only `active` custom domains can be made primary — the request fails with 409 otherwise. Any previous primary is cleared in the same transaction.
tools.name: websiteDomains_setPrimaryDomain
tools.title: Set the primary custom domain

tools.description: Deregisters the hostname from the Cactal edge and deletes the domain record. If the removed domain was primary, the oldest remaining active custom domain is promoted automatically. If edge deregistration fails, the domain stays in `removing` status and a background sweep retries until it is gone. Platform subdomains cannot be removed.
tools.name: websiteDomains_removeCustomDomain
tools.title: Remove a custom domain

tools.description: Moves the website to `<label>.<platform domain>`, the free address every website is allocated at creation. `label` is just the leading part: 1-40 characters, lowercase letters, digits, and inner hyphens, and it may not be one of the labels Cactal reserves. The change takes effect immediately, on published and draft hosts alike. The previous hostname is released at the same moment, with no redirect and no grace period, so any existing links to it break and another website may claim it. Take care on a published site. Fails with 409 when the label is already taken by another website; renaming to the label the website already has is a no-op. Custom domains are unaffected, and if one of them is primary it stays the canonical address.
tools.name: websiteDomains_renamePlatformDomain
tools.title: Rename the platform subdomain

tools.description: Returns ready assets newest first as compact rows (`description`, `category`, dimensions, `url`, `srcSet`); fetch one asset for `originalUrl` and `variants`. Filter by `kind`, `category`, `type` (the broad MIME family: image, video, audio, font, or document), or `search`, which prefix-matches each term against the filename, description, and category; every term must match, else any term. Page size defaults to 50 (max 100).

search.description: Matches filename, description, and category; each term matches as a prefix.

type.description: Broad file type derived from the MIME type: image, video, audio, font, or document (everything else). Combines with kind, category, and search.

tools.name: websiteAssets_list
tools.title: List or search assets

tools.description: Returns the asset with `description`, `category`, and its CDN delivery shape: for transformable images `url` is the optimized 1920px default and `originalUrl` the original bytes; both never expire. MCP clients that render images also receive the image.
tools.name: websiteAssets_get
tools.title: Get an asset

tools.description: Fetches 1-10 public http(s) URLs server-side, one at a time, and stores each as a ready asset with no upload or finalize step. Media only: images, fonts, PDF, audio, video, dotLottie, and Rive; text, data, documents, and archives are refused. Images, fonts, and PDFs must parse as what they claim, hosts on private addresses are rejected, the upload kind and MIME rules apply, and each download is capped at 30 MiB (larger files must be uploaded directly). Each item may carry a `description` and, for images, a `category`. Name each item by `url`, or by `photo`: the number over a picture on contact sheets `webResearch.profile` or `webResearch.viewImage` showed you, which saves copying its long signed link. `assets` carries successes with CDN URLs and `sourceUrl`; `errors` carries failures typed `invalid_url`, `non_public_address`, `unreachable`, `too_large`, `unsupported_type`, `signature_expired`, or `unknown_photo` (a number you were not shown or that expired; look at the pictures again for current numbers). Import only assets you have the right to use.

items.description: Each item succeeds or fails on its own.

category.description: What the image is. Images only.

description.description: One sentence: subject, visible text, style, intended use.

filename.description: Stored filename; defaults to the URL path segment.

photo.description: Instead of `url`: the number over a picture on contact sheets `webResearch.profile` or `webResearch.viewImage` showed you.

url.description: Public http(s) URL of the file to import.

tools.name: websiteAssets_importFromUrl
tools.title: Import assets from public URLs

tools.description: Changes `filename`, `description`, or `category`. Pass only the fields to change; `null` clears a field. `category` is images only.

anyOf.description: What the image is. Images only.
One sentence: subject, visible text, style, intended use.

tools.name: websiteAssets_update

tools.description: Archives the asset: it immediately stops appearing in list responses and its id returns 404 from every asset endpoint. Archival cannot be undone through the API; previously issued CDN URLs keep serving the file.
tools.name: websiteAssets_delete
tools.title: Delete an asset

tools.description: Returns the website’s durable project knowledge: the text the user maintains as `content`, plus the `agentNotes` Cactal distills from agent conversations. Both are included in every Cactal agent request. Read them before working on a website.
tools.name: websiteKnowledge_project_get
tools.title: Get project knowledge

tools.description: Applies exact-match text edits to the user’s project knowledge text, in order; an empty `oldStr` appends. Change it only when the user asks; agent-discovered facts belong in agent notes. A passage that no longer matches fails with `validation` and returns the current content.

edits.description: Edits applied in order against the evolving text.

oldStr.description: Exact text to find. Must match exactly once unless `replaceAll` is `true`. Empty appends `newStr` to the end.

replaceAll.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring a unique match.

tools.name: websiteKnowledge_project_edit
tools.title: Edit project knowledge

tools.description: Applies exact-match text edits to the agent notes, in order; an empty `oldStr` appends. Record only durable facts, decisions, rejected directions, and constraints, one short line each, never progress logs or anything derivable from the website source. A passage that no longer matches fails with `validation` and returns the current notes.

edits.description: Edits applied in order against the evolving text.

oldStr.description: Exact text to find. Must match exactly once unless `replaceAll` is `true`. Empty appends `newStr` to the end.

replaceAll.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring a unique match.

tools.name: websiteKnowledge_agentNotes_edit
tools.title: Edit agent notes

tools.description: Lists the website’s private durable context entries: uploaded files and pasted text, each with a `title`, a generated `description`, and an `origin` of `upload` or `text`.
tools.name: websiteKnowledge_list
tools.title: List project context

tools.description: Keeps pasted or typed text as a context entry the agent searches and reads when relevant, using one of the website’s 25 slots. Cactal titles and describes it. Use this for material the user gives you to keep; your own findings belong in agent notes.

text.description: The text to keep, as plain text or Markdown.

tools.name: websiteKnowledge_create
tools.title: Add project context from text

tools.description: Renames a context entry or replaces the text the agent reads. Replacing text does not change the downloadable original; images have no text.

text.description: Replaces the text the agent reads; images have none.

tools.name: websiteKnowledge_update
tools.title: Update project context entry

tools.description: Read a bounded line range from a project context document. Read short relevant documents directly; search large documents first. Do not reread sufficient search passages.
tools.name: websiteKnowledge_read
tools.title: Read project context resource

tools.description: Find evidence across selected project context documents. Batch independent queries; use passages directly when sufficient. Results merge overlapping text and include source ranges and zero-based queryIndexes into queries. matched reports a hit; truncated means evidence may be omitted, clipped means partial lines, and unavailableResourceIds were not searched. Resolve missing evidence before concluding a fact is absent.

maxCharacters.description: Shared passage character budget across all documents and queries.

queries.description: Independent case-insensitive literal terms matched within a line, not questions or regular expressions.

resourceIds.description: Selected text resource ids from the project context index, in relevance order.

tools.title: Search project context documents

tools.description: Returns one private PNG, JPEG, or WebP context resource.

tools.description: Lists file identities, sizes, and line counts without contents, sorted by type then name with cursor pagination (default 20, maximum 100). Filter by name with `nameGlob`. Defaults to head; pass `target=published` or an explicit `version`, and pin continuation requests to the resolved response version.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from the previous page. Continue with the returned resolved version to keep the listing pinned.

limit.description: Maximum files to return. Defaults to 20 and cannot exceed 100.

nameGlob.description: Only list files whose name matches this glob. `*` and `?` stop at a `/` segment boundary; `**` crosses them, for example `blog/**`.

version.description: Explicit source version. Takes precedence over `target`.

tools.title: List source files

tools.description: Reads up to 50 files by name from head, published, or an explicit version. A single-file read supports line and character ranges; continue truncated reads with `nextStartCharacter` and the resolved `version`.

endCharacter.description: Last character to return from the selected line range (1-based, inclusive). Only valid when reading a single file.

endLine.description: Last line to return (1-based, inclusive). Only valid when reading a single file.

names.description: File names to read (up to 50). Singleton files are addressed by their type name, for example `global_css`.

startCharacter.description: First character to return from the selected line range (1-based, inclusive). Only valid when reading a single file.

startLine.description: First line to return (1-based, inclusive). Only valid when reading a single file.

version.description: Explicit source version. Takes precedence over `target`.

tools.name: websiteSourceCode_files_read
tools.title: Read source files

tools.description: Finds text across every source file and returns one entry per matching line with its file name, line, and column. Call this first to locate code, then read only the files it names with websiteSourceCode.files.read. `pattern` is literal text unless `isRegex` is set, and matching is line by line, so a pattern cannot span a newline. Narrow with `nameGlob` and `type`, ask for surrounding lines with `contextLines`, or set `filesOnly` for the cheapest orientation. Results are cursor-paginated over matches.

contextLines.description: Surrounding lines to return on each side of a match (0 to 3). Defaults to 0.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from the previous page. Pass the returned `version` too to keep the search pinned.

filesOnly.description: Return one entry per matching file, with no line detail.

isRegex.description: Read `pattern` as a regular expression. JavaScript syntax works, including `\b`, `\d`, lookahead, and lazy quantifiers; named capture groups are not supported.

limit.description: Maximum matches to return per page. Defaults to 20, maximum 100.

maxMatchesPerFile.description: Maximum matches from any one file (up to 50). Defaults to 10.

nameGlob.description: Only search names matching this glob. `*` and `?` stop at a `/`; `**` crosses them, for example `blog/**`.

pattern.description: Text to find. Literal unless `isRegex` is set. Matched line by line, so `^` and `$` anchor to line boundaries and a pattern cannot span a newline.

type.description: Only search files of this type.

version.description: Explicit source version. Takes precedence over `target`.

tools.title: Search source files

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from the previous page. Continue with the returned resolved versions to keep the comparison pinned.

from.description: Base side of the diff: a version number, `head`, or `published`. Defaults to `published`.

limit.description: Maximum candidate files to compare. Defaults to 20 and cannot exceed 20.

to.description: Target side of the diff: a version number, `head`, or `published`. Defaults to `head`.

tools.name: websiteSourceCode_changes_list
tools.title: List changed source files

tools.description: Returns a bounded unified diff for one file name between two version refs, defaulting from published to head.

from.description: Base side of the diff: a version number, `head`, or `published`. Defaults to `published`.

to.description: Target side of the diff: a version number, `head`, or `published`. Defaults to `head`.

tools.name: websiteSourceCode_files_diff
tools.title: Diff one source file

tools.title: Create or update a source file

Each `oldStr` must match once unless `replaceAll` is true, and any failing edit aborts the whole call. Set `dryRun` to validate and count replacements without committing. Takes the edit lease when no `leaseToken` is sent.

dryRun.description: Validate every edit and report the replacement counts without committing.

files.description: Files to edit (up to 50, and 200 edits in total). Every edit across every file commits as one version, or none of them do.

edits.description: Edits applied in order against the evolving content of this file.

oldStr.description: Exact text to find. Must match exactly once unless `replaceAll` is `true`.

replaceAll.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring a unique match.

name.description: Name of the file to edit. Singleton files are addressed by their type name, for example `global_css`.

leaseToken.description: Omit to have Cactal take the edit lease for you; pass a token from websiteSourceCode.lease.acquire to take over from another editor.

tools.title: Edit source files with string replacement

tools.description: Deletes one head file while preserving history. Address named files by `type` and `name`, and singletons by `type`; takes the edit lease when no `leaseToken` is sent.

leaseToken.description: Omit to have Cactal take the edit lease for you; pass a token from websiteSourceCode.lease.acquire to take over from another editor.

tools.title: Delete a source file

tools.title: Edit a page route

page.description: Page to edit. Omit to edit the site-wide default metadata in `website_config`.

tools.name: websiteSourceCode_metadata_edit
tools.title: Edit page or site metadata

Failures return `ok: false` with diagnostics, and pages that compiled but threw while rendering in `renderFailures`. No lease is required and no CMS content is read, so the outcome depends only on source and schema.
tools.name: websiteSourceCode_head_check
tools.title: Validate the head source

tools.title: Restore head to a previous state

tools.title: Roll back to a previous version

tools.description: Renders one page of the site in a real browser and returns the image, so you can check layout, spacing, and responsive behaviour that source-level checks cannot see. `path` is site-relative and may include a query string, so dynamic routes are captured with real values rather than placeholders. Focus the capture with `selector` (plus optional `padding` for surrounding context) or a `clip` rectangle in CSS pixels from the top-left of the page; the region is scrolled into view and captured within the configured viewport, so it must fit inside it, and these options exclude each other and `fullPage`. Fonts, images, and (for `fullPage`) lazy content are awaited before the capture, and CSS animations are fast-forwarded to their end state by default. Fails with 409 when the draft build is still in progress or has failed; poll `websiteSourceCode.deployment.status` and retry.

clip.description: Crop to this rectangle, in CSS pixels from the top-left of the rendered page at the chosen viewport; it is scrolled into view and must fit within the viewport. Only for regions no selector frames.

colorScheme.description: Browser color preference to emulate. Omit it to use the renderer default.

delayMs.description: Extra settle time before capturing, in milliseconds.

freezeAnimations.description: Fast-forward CSS animations and transitions to their end state so captures are deterministic.

fullPage.description: Capture the whole scrollable page instead of just the viewport. Excludes `selector` and `clip`.

padding.description: CSS pixels of surrounding page to include on every side of the `selector` match.

path.description: Site-relative path to render, including any query string, e.g. `/blog/my-post`.

scrollTo.description: Scroll to a CSS selector or an absolute Y offset before capturing.

selector.description: Crop to the first element matching this CSS selector, scrolled into view. Preferred: it follows the layout at every viewport.

target.description: `head` renders the current draft; `published` renders the live site.

waitForSelector.description: Wait for this CSS selector to match before capturing.

tools.name: websitePreview_capture
tools.title: Capture a page screenshot

tools.description: Returns every active collection and field of a website in one call — the full content model. Collections are ordered newest first; fields are grouped by collection in display order. Use this to discover the schema before reading or writing items.
tools.name: cms_schema_snapshot
tools.title: Get the CMS schema snapshot

tools.description: Creates a collection in the website’s CMS. `slug` uses lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens (max 64 characters, starting with a letter) and must be unique among the website’s active collections; `displayName` is 1–200 characters and `description` up to 2,000. Optionally pass `fields` (up to 100, same shape as the create-field body) to define the schema in the same call. A website can hold at most 100 active collections; the limit is enforced with a conflict error.
tools.name: cms_collections_create
tools.title: Create a collection

tools.description: Updates `displayName` (1–200 characters), `description` (up to 2,000 characters; pass `null` to clear), and/or `slug` (a rename). A slug change fails with a conflict when another active collection in the website already uses it, and when the website has a published version the rename is validated against the published site’s content queries and rejected when it would break them.

slug.description: New slug for the collection — a rename. Omit to keep the current slug. Must be unique among the website’s active collections; when the website has a published version the rename is validated against the published site’s content queries.

tools.name: cms_collections_update
tools.title: Update a collection

tools.description: Soft-deletes the collection, making it and all of its items unreachable through the API; the slug becomes reusable. Refused with a conflict while any reference field in another collection targets this collection — delete those fields first. If the website has a published version, the deletion is validated against the published site’s content queries and rejected when the site still depends on the collection.
tools.name: cms_collections_delete
tools.title: Delete a collection

tools.description: Adds a typed field at the end of the collection’s field order. `key` is lowercase snake_case (max 64 characters), must be unique in the collection, and cannot use the reserved metadata names `id`, `slug`, `publishedAt`, `publishAt`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, or `position`; `type` is immutable after creation. `reference` and `multi_reference` fields require a `targetCollectionId` in the same website, and `option` fields require `config.choices` (1–1,000 choices). A collection can hold at most 100 fields, and `required: true` is rejected while the collection has active items — add the field as optional, backfill every item, then mark it required.
tools.name: cms_fields_create
tools.title: Add a field to a collection

tools.description: Updates `displayName`, `description`, `required`, `isUnique`, `example`, and (for `option` fields only) `config`; `type` and `targetCollectionId` are immutable. Setting `required: true` is rejected until every active item has a valid value for the field. Setting `isUnique: true` enforces uniqueness on all future writes and fails with a conflict when existing values already collide; unique is not supported for `plain_text`, `markdown`, `multi_reference`, `image`, `gallery`, or `file` fields. Pass `key` to rename the field’s key: the key is atomically migrated in every stored item’s `data` in the same transaction (no values are lost), a conflict is returned when the new key is already used in the collection, and when the website has a published version the rename is validated against the published site’s content queries. Pass `position: "first"` or `"last"`, or `"before"` / `"after"` together with `anchorFieldId`, to move the field within the collection’s display order.

anchorFieldId.description: Sibling field to move against when `position` is `"before"` or `"after"`.

key.description: New key for the field — a rename. Omit to keep the current key. Atomically migrates the key in every stored item’s `data`, so no values are lost.

position.description: Moves the field within the collection’s display order. Omit to leave the order unchanged. `"before"` / `"after"` require `anchorFieldId`.

tools.name: cms_fields_update
tools.title: Update a field

tools.description: Permanently deletes the field and its stored values: the key is stripped from every item’s `data`, and reference or asset attachments made through the field are removed. This cannot be undone. If the website has a published version, the deletion is validated against the published site’s content queries and rejected when the site still depends on the field.
tools.name: cms_fields_delete
tools.title: Delete a field

tools.description: Returns the collection’s active items in manual (drag) order by default, 20 per page (max 100); paginate with `cursor` or with 1-based `page` offsets, not both. Filter with `published` (`true` / `false`) and a JSON-encoded `filter` map of `{ fieldKey: { operator: value } }` — operators `eq`, `neq`, `in`, `nin`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `contains`, `startsWith`, `endsWith`, and `exists`, plus `slug` equality on reference fields; metadata keys are `id`, `slug`, `publishedAt`, `publishAt`, `createdAt`, and `updatedAt`. Combine clauses with `filterLogic` (`and` by default, or `or`). `search` accepts a query string (1–200 characters) or JSON `{ "query", "fields" }` to restrict which text fields are searched; `sort` accepts JSON `{ "kind": "field" | "meta", "field", "direction": "asc" | "desc" }`, where sortable metadata fields are `id`, `slug`, `publishedAt`, `publishAt`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, and `position`. `depth` (0–3, default 0) embeds referenced items in place of their ids, one level per unit.
tools.name: cms_items_list
tools.title: List items in a collection

tools.description: Returns one item, looked up by `itemId` or by the `collectionId` + `slug` pair (provide exactly one of the two). The `data` object is complete and schema-shaped: every currently-defined field is present and missing optional values read as `null`. `depth` (0–3, default 0) embeds referenced items in place of their ids, one level per unit; referenced items that were deleted read as `null` (single reference) or are omitted from arrays (multi-reference). Set `published` to `"true"` or `"false"` to match only a published or only a draft item (a mismatch reads as not found). List items that reference it with `cms.items.backreferences.list`.

collectionId.description: Collection to look the item up in by slug. Pair with `slug`.

itemId.description: Item id. Provide either this or the `collectionId` + `slug` pair.

published.description: Only match a published (`"true"`) or draft (`"false"`) item; a mismatch reads as not found. Omit to match either.

slug.description: Item slug within the collection. Pair with `collectionId`.

tools.name: cms_items_get
tools.title: Get an item

tools.description: Lists active items that reference the target item through a `reference` or `multi_reference` field, newest first, with cursor pagination (default 20 per page, maximum 100). Each source item appears once even when multiple fields point to the target. `depth` (0–3, default 0) controls reference hydration in the returned source items.
tools.name: cms_items_backreferences_list
tools.title: List item backreferences

tools.description: Creates an item at the end of the collection’s manual order. Scalar values go in `data` keyed by field key and are validated against the field types — unknown keys are rejected, required fields must be present, `plain_text` and `markdown` are capped at 1,048,576 bytes (markdown must not contain raw HTML), `date` values are ISO 8601 with timezone, and `color` values are normalized to hex. Relationship and asset values go in the side maps: `references` (`reference`: an item id; `multi_reference`: an ordered array of up to 1,000 ids), `images` (`image`: an asset id or `{ assetId, altText }`; `gallery`: an ordered array of up to 25 of those), and `files` (`file`: an asset id or `{ assetId }`). `slug` is optional — it is derived from `data.title` or `data.name` when omitted. Set a non-future `publishedAt` to create an already-published item, or a future `publishAt` to schedule it; the two fields are mutually exclusive.

publishAt.description: Future absolute timestamp for scheduled publication. Cannot be combined with `publishedAt`.

publishedAt.description: Initial publication timestamp. Must not be in the future. Omit for a draft, or use `publishAt` to schedule publication.

tools.name: cms_items_create
tools.title: Create an item

tools.description: Patches an item; omitted fields are left untouched. Keys in `data` are merged into the existing values and validated the same way as on create, while each key provided in `references`, `images`, or `files` replaces that field’s value wholesale — pass `null` (or `[]` for multi-valued fields) to clear an optional field. `slug` renames the item’s slug; slug and unique-field collisions fail with a conflict. Pass `position: "first"` or `"last"`, or `"before"` / `"after"` together with `anchorItemId`, to move the item within the collection’s manual order — the default sort for item lists.

anchorItemId.description: Sibling item to move against when `position` is `"before"` or `"after"`.

position.description: Moves the item within the collection’s manual order — the default sort for item lists. Omit to leave the order unchanged. `"before"` / `"after"` require `anchorItemId`.

slug.description: New slug for the item — a rename. Omit to keep the current slug. Must be unique among the collection’s active items.

tools.name: cms_items_update
tools.title: Update an item

tools.description: Use exactly one publication action: `published: true` publishes immediately and sets `publishedAt` to now; a future `publishAt` schedules a draft for automatic publication; `published: false` unpublishes an item or cancels its schedule. A published item must be unpublished before it can be scheduled because CMS items do not have revision snapshots. Published websites read only items with an actual `publishedAt`, so immediate and scheduled promotion become visible without a site republish. Repeating the same action is idempotent.

publishAt.description: Future absolute timestamp for scheduling. Omit `published`; scheduled items remain hidden until the promotion job runs.

published.description: `true` publishes immediately; `false` unpublishes or cancels a schedule. Use `publishAt` instead to schedule publication.

tools.name: cms_items_setPublished
tools.title: Publish, schedule, or unpublish an item

tools.description: Soft-deletes the item: it disappears from reads, list results, and backreferences, and fields referencing it read `null` (single reference) or shrink (multi-reference). Its slug becomes reusable, and incoming references are preserved so the item can be restored.
tools.name: cms_items_delete
tools.title: Delete an item

tools.description: Restores a soft-deleted item, making it readable again and re-exposing references to and from it. Returns 404 when the item is not currently deleted.
tools.name: cms_items_restore
tools.title: Restore a deleted item

tools.description: Returns aggregate engagement totals — page views, distinct visitors, visits, bounces, and total time in seconds — for a date range, optionally broken down by one dimension. Use it to answer "how much traffic did the site get" and "what are the top pages/referrers/countries" style questions; use the timeseries endpoint when you need values over time instead. `startAt` and `endAt` are Unix epoch milliseconds; optional filter parameters (path, referrer, country, event, UTM fields, ...) narrow the data. Without `dimension` the response carries the totals alone. With `dimension` (e.g. `path` for top pages, `referrer` for top referrers, `country` for top countries) the response also carries `rows`: up to `limit` (default 25, max 1000) values of that dimension ranked by page views, each with its own engagement totals. Requires a plan that includes analytics (403 otherwise); all-zero totals until the website is published and has traffic.

dimension.description: Break the range down by this dimension, e.g. `path` for top pages, `referrer` for top referrers, `country` for top countries. Omit for totals only.

limit.description: Maximum number of dimension rows to return (default 25, max 1000). Only used when `dimension` is set.

tools.name: websiteAnalytics_query_get
tools.title: Query analytics totals and breakdowns

tools.description: Returns one traffic time series bucketed by `unit` (`year`, `month`, `day`, `hour`, or `minute`). `series` selects which: `pageviews` returns parallel `pageviews` and `sessions` arrays with one point per time bucket (and accepts `compare` — `prev` or `yoy` — to request comparison data for the previous period or year), while `events` returns tracked custom-event counts as one `events` point per event name per time bucket. Only the requested series' fields are present in the response. `startAt` and `endAt` are Unix epoch milliseconds; `timezone` is an IANA name (e.g. `America/New_York`) that controls bucket boundaries; optional filter parameters narrow the data. The series is capped to the most recent `maxPoints` time buckets (default 30, max 500); a `truncated` field reports when the cap was applied. Requires a plan that includes analytics (403 otherwise); empty until the website is published and has traffic.

compare.description: Request comparison data alongside the primary series: `prev` for the previous period, `yoy` for the same range one year earlier. Only valid when `series` is `pageviews`.

series.description: Which time series to return: `pageviews` for page views and sessions per bucket, `events` for tracked custom-event counts per event name per bucket.

tools.name: websiteAnalytics_timeseries_get
tools.title: Get an analytics time series

tools.description: Returns a compact snapshot of traffic over Umami's trailing 30-minute realtime window: total page views, distinct visitors, tracked custom events, and distinct countries, plus the snapshot timestamp. The visitor total is not directly comparable to the removed `active` endpoint's five-minute count. Use it to see recent activity; use the query endpoint for historical ranges. Requires a plan that includes analytics (403 otherwise); all-zero totals until the website is published and has traffic.
tools.name: websiteAnalytics_realtime_get
tools.title: Get a realtime traffic snapshot

tools.description: Returns every form with inbox and spam counts, whether the published site still references it, who it notifies, the number of inbox submissions since the caller last opened the Forms tab, and monthly usage against the Free plan limit (`limit` is null on paid plans). Forms come from `<form method="post" action="/_cactal/forms/<name>">` in the website source and appear here as soon as the draft or published build contains them, before any submission.

Items carry the fields in submitted order, the inferred submitter email and name, page, spam signals, classifier verdict, and notification state. Submission data is personal information: never render it on the public website.

form.description: Only submissions of this form name.

source.description: `published` for real visitors, `draft` for test submissions from the draft preview.

status.description: `spam` hides the submission in the spam folder; `inbox` restores it and sends any missed notification.

Capture your own website with `websitePreview.capture`. Charged in AI credits to the website's organization.

clip.description: Crop to this rectangle, in CSS pixels from the top-left of the rendered page at the chosen viewport; it is scrolled into view and must fit within the viewport. Only for regions no selector frames.

delayMs.description: Extra settle time before capturing, in milliseconds.

freezeAnimations.description: Fast-forward CSS animations and transitions to their end state so captures are deterministic.

padding.description: CSS pixels of surrounding page to include on every side of the `selector` match.

scrollTo.description: Scroll to a CSS selector or an absolute Y offset before capturing.

selector.description: Crop to the first element matching this CSS selector, scrolled into view. Preferred: it follows the layout at every viewport.

url.description: Absolute public http(s) URL of the page to capture.

waitForSelector.description: Wait for this CSS selector to match before capturing.
